text:
maya: FYI I'm starting a 5% canary for model v3.2-quant8 now. Want to validate both perf and quality gates before promoting. Key signals: p95 latency, hallucination_rate (eval harness), and answer_quality (annotated testset + micro human eval).

deploy-bot: deploy triggered for canary group=5% by maya — build: v3.2-quant8 — job: canary-rollout-1912345678

devin: can you paste the concrete thresholds we'll use for auto-fallback? also how long is the observation window?

maya: proposal: minimum 3k queries or 2 hours (whichever first) before any auto-promote. Auto-fallback triggers if BOTH: quality_delta_abs >= 1.0% (worse) AND p95_latency increase >= 25ms relative to baseline. Immediate abort if hallucination_rate > 2.5%. We'll also require statistical significance using sequential test (SPRT) to avoid noise.

sam: SPRT sounds good. can we also add a minimum relative lift floor so tiny deltas don't cause churn? e.g., change must be >= 0.5% AND p<0.05 per SPRT to count. Otherwise mark as inconclusive and hold.

eva: strongly agree on tying quality + latency. ops note: need to ensure fallback path is fast — we should revert routing before dropping commitment pools. Also add a canary holdback flag to keep 20% traffic pinned to baseline for 24h after promote.

ricardo: offline eval numbers: on our 12k evaluation prompts v3.2-quant8 shows -1.6% answer_quality and +18ms p95 on average. But variance is high on shorter prompts. I will push a stratified breakdown to the eval dashboard.

maya: thanks — that delta is right in the danger zone. Given that, I'm lowering promote target: require observed quality_delta_abs < 0.75% AND no hallucination spike, and require SPRT p<0.05 with min_samples=3000. If inconclusive after 6 hours we auto-hold and ping team.

sam: small suggestion: implement a rolling baseline update so the comparator adapts slowly. Otherwise we might bias against steady drift. Set baseline_alpha=0.05 (EWMA).

platform-bot: suggested rollout config for eng-platform service (snippet):
```
{
  "policy": "sequential_canary",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "min_samples": 3000,
  "observation_window": "6h",
  "quality_metric": "answer_quality",
  "quality_delta_threshold_pct": 0.75,
  "hallucination_threshold_pct": 2.5,
  "latency_metric": "p95_ms",
  "latency_delta_threshold_ms": 25,
  "fallback_condition": "(quality_delta_abs >= 1.0 AND p95_delta_ms >= 25) OR hallucination_rate > 2.5",
  "stat_test": "SPRT",
  "stat_p_threshold": 0.05,
  "holdback_after_promote": 20,
  "baseline_ewma_alpha": 0.05
}
```

devin: looks good. can platform add a debug endpoint to show current SPRT state (accept/continue/reject) per canary? Last time we lost context when the test flipped.

platform-bot: yes, will add /rollout/{id}/stats endpoint. also logging will include sample counts and z-scores for audit.

maya: ok let's run this config for the canary. Quick checklist: 1) ensure annotated eval set is uploaded (ricardo), 2) enable SPRT logging (platform), 3) ops on standby for manual rollback if auto-fallback triggers unexpectedly (eva).

ops-bot: alerting rule created: alert if fallback_condition evaluates true for >5 consecutive minutes. Notifying #eng-oncall.

ricardo: uploaded stratified eval CSV to drive and added a short README on notable prompt classes (short prompts, code, multi-turn). Link: https://redwood-internal/drive/evals/v3.2-quant8-strata

maya: thanks. will wait for at least 3k samples or 2h before decisions. tagging @sam @devin for quick review if we hit the inconclusive state. :thumbsup:
